dimensions.note: Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). credentials-sensitive-field on secretDestination re-examined and accepted inline with a reason: the field holds the op://<vaultId>/<itemId>/<fieldLabel> pointer that deliverSecret builds from IDs and a label, never the key. toKeyResource is the only snapshot mapper and never reads applicationKey; tests assert the serialized snapshot excludes the secret and (new) that secretDestination equals the expected pointer. Marking it sensitive would vault a locator and break CEL lookups. One real exposure path was found and closed: when delivery to 1Password Connect fails, create embeds connectFetch's message, which carries Connect's response body verbatim, in the thrown error that reaches run logs and reports. Connect is not known to echo submitted values, but the secret is now scrubbed from that message; a new test with an echoing 400 body fails without the scrub and passes with it.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. Every method logs entry and completion with structured placeholders — logger.info("...{field}", { field }) — and no logger call uses a template literal. Completion lines carry enough to distinguish outcomes.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. b2Fetch attaches status and B2 code to the thrown error rather than collapsing to a string, retries only 429/503/500 with bounded backoff honoring Retry-After, and re-authorizes exactly once on 401 expired_auth_token. A 401 from a missing capability is explicitly not transient and is never retried.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. 44 tests, all mocked, plus a full live cycle against real B2: a genuine application key minted scoped to a scratch bucket with a 1h self-expiry, its secret delivered to 1Password Connect and asserted CONCEALED there, provably absent from every swamp snapshot, then revoked — with the second delete succeeding as an idempotent already-absent. Live verification also confirmed the .2 bucketIds fix: a real key returned an array.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. delete is idempotent and verifies the key exists via b2_list_keys first, because B2 documents no key-not-found error for b2_delete_key — treating a generic 400 bad_request as already-gone would swallow real request bugs. It refuses to claim absence when the listing was truncated. create refuses a name clash by default, since B2 key names are not identifiers and a duplicate would leave the first key live and unreachable.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. Audited before the repository was made public: every identifier in code, tests and docs is a fixture. All 74 real identifiers extracted from a live account scan were cross-checked against every blob in git history with zero matches. Real scan output lives under .swamp/, which is gitignored with no tracked files. Smoke-test model instances take their targets through env references so no real bucket name or key ID is committed.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. bucketIds is now a plain array rather than nullable: b2_list_keys has no "unknown" case, so an omitted field means account-wide and is recorded as []. This removes a null-handling trap and, more importantly, ends a disagreement with b2-account, which already encoded the same B2 field as an array — two models describing one key must not describe it differently.

Delta review for 2026.10.22.1 (hygiene cards #435/#436). Carried from the 2026.08.05.3 review; code for this dimension unchanged since (git log), and not re-reviewed in this delta. sync, create, delete. No update method, deliberately: B2 application keys are immutable — changing scope means minting a new key and revoking the old one, which is a workflow spanning two objects, not a model method.
